**Ch 076 Draft — checks**

The Flask speech compresses the source's two separate paragraphs (Flask's superstition line, then the Fedallah-tusk observation) into one speech. In the source Flask says: *"did you never hear, Stubb, that that ship can never afterwards capsize?"* — then separately raises the tusk. In the draft Flask says: *"Did you ever notice how that tusk of his—a long tooth, carved somehow into a snake's head—is a sort of omen?"* The source's version is: *"Did you ever notice how that tusk of his is a sort of carved into a snake's head, Stubb?"* — which is just an observation with no "omen" gloss. That's a minor paraphrase, not a structural damage.

The Stubb speech in the source has a clear two-part structure: (a) "I never look at him at all; but if ever I get a chance of a dark night…" and then (b) the devil story about John. In the draft these are reversed and merged: the devil/John story comes first, then "But I never look at Fedallah at all; if ever I get a chance of a dark night…" The "Aye, will I!" now dangles as a conclusion without the setup of *what* Stubb intends to do (throw Fedallah overboard) — but within the draft passage, the reader has just been told "giving Fedallah a sea-toss" in Flask's next speech, so context recovers it. Borderline, but the reader isn't truly confused about what "Aye, will I!" means — it follows "look down there, Flask" pointing to the sea.

Flask's line *"But Stubb, you boasted of giving Fedallah a sea-toss; if he's going to live for ever, what good will pitching him overboard do?"* — in the source this follows a long exchange where Stubb establishes Fedallah's infinite age (the mainmast/hoops speech) and then Stubb's threat is registered. In the draft that age-establishing speech is cut, so Flask's "if he's going to live for ever" has no antecedent in the draft. A competent reader would not know Stubb had just argued Fedallah lives forever — that exchange was removed. This is a **broken pivot**: the "if he's going to live for ever" clause depends on a two-sided structure (Stubb's age-claim → Flask's rebuttal) where the first side was cut.

Everything else in Ch 076 parses cleanly.
